name: android_resource_rules
notes: Data-driven rules for Android resource containers: resources.arsc (ResTable chunks), AndroidManifest.xml (binary AXML) and APK-level signing artifacts. Vendor-agnostic: SDK rules are inventory-only, tamper rules are shape-based. No regex is used anywhere so the file stays free of escape sequences and is safe to hand-edit. Manifest thresholds are calibrated against a single measured clean manifest; treat them as provisional until more baselines are added.

rules.label: AppLovin MAX mediation
rules.notes: Mediation layer. Presence of the creative debugger UI package means a full SDK, not a stub.

rules.label: Yandex Mobile Ads
rules.notes: Often bundled as an AppLovin or IronSource mediation adapter for CIS traffic.

rules.label: Google Mobile Ads / AdMob
rules.notes: Resource-level only. The App ID normally lives in the manifest as a meta-data value.

rules.label: Firebase Crashlytics
rules.notes: The build_id resource is unique per build and is a reliable build-identity anchor.

rules.label: Unity engine (inferred from resources)
rules.notes: Lets the engine be identified without opening a single native library. Cross-check with the native ruleset.

rules.label: Flutter (inferred from resources)
rules.notes: Confirm against libflutter.so and libapp.so in the native ruleset.

rules.label: React Native (inferred from resources)
rules.notes: Pair with libhermes.so or libjsc.so detection.

rules.label: Firebase Realtime Database endpoint
rules.notes: The project host is a strong identity anchor: it survives repacking and ties a mod back to the original app.

rules.label: Google OAuth client ID shipped in resources
rules.notes: Expected for Play Games sign-in, but the client list is a build fingerprint. Multiple IDs usually mean debug plus release.

rules.label: Helpshift in-app support
rules.notes: The tenant subdomain names the publisher and is useful for attributing an unknown build.

rules.label: Google Play services base module
rules.notes: Ships a large localized string block. Its locale coverage is a good baseline for locale-stripping heuristics.

rules.label: Material Components for Android
rules.notes: Indicates a standard Gradle plus AGP build even when the app itself is an engine game.

rules.label: AndroidX App Startup initializer
rules.notes: Provider authority suffix. Its authority prefix must equal the application id; a mismatch is a rename signal.

rules.label: Chinese-language SDK error strings
rules.notes: Marks a bundled CN vendor SDK. Misspelled keys such as conent_type are stable, high-signal anchors.

rules.label: Application label diverges in a subset of locales
rules.notes: Resolve app_name for every locale config. Genuine builds translate the label or keep it identical; a build that keeps the original name everywhere except one or two locales is being rebranded for a specific audience while staying unremarkable elsewhere.

rules.label: Application label differs from baseline while package name is unchanged
rules.notes: Classic soft rebrand: identical application id so updates and save data still line up, new display name so the build looks like a different product.

rules.label: Identical resource key pool but different value pool
rules.notes: Same resource names, same entry counts, different string values means nothing was recompiled from sources: the table was edited in place. Strongest single repack signal available from resources.arsc alone.

rules.label: Manifest package differs from ResTable package name
rules.notes: The canonical package-rename detector. A rename done with a manifest editor rarely updates the ResTable package name, so the two disagree.

rules.label: Provider authority prefix does not match the application id
rules.notes: AGP derives authorities such as the startup initializer from the application id. After a rename the old prefix is usually left behind.

rules.label: Declared component lives outside the application package
rules.notes: Recalibrated against a measured clean build, where this rule produced six false positives out of six matches: five were ordinary bundled SDK components (Play Billing, Play services, datatransport) and one was an R8-repackaged Application class. Do not fire on prefix mismatch alone. Skip exclude_prefixes, skip classes whose package looks machine-generated, and require corroboration: a matching foreign JNI export prefix, a foreign host string, or a foreign provider authority.

rules.label: Non-vendor host string next to original vendor hosts
rules.notes: Compare the registrable domain of every host string against the domain implied by the application id. A redirect target usually sits right next to the untouched original endpoints.

rules.label: Locale value table rewritten or collapsed
rules.notes: Locale configs survive but their values are replaced by copies of a neighbouring locale, so translated strings disappear and duplicates appear. Typical of a table rebuilt by a third-party tool rather than aapt2.

rules.label: Non-standard ResTable package id
rules.notes: Application packages use 0x7f and the framework uses 0x01. Other ids mean a shared library, an overlay, or a hand-patched table.

rules.label: APK Signing Block present but no v1 signature files
rules.notes: Legitimate for a modern minSdk 24+ build. Becomes a strong repack signal when the baseline shipped v1 files and the sample does not, which is exactly what signature-stripping patchers produce.

rules.label: Neither APK Signing Block nor v1 signature files
rules.notes: The archive cannot be installed as is. Almost always an intermediate artifact from a patch pipeline that has not been re-signed yet.

rules.label: Signed with the Android debug certificate
rules.notes: The debug key is shared by every SDK install, so it provides no authorship guarantee whatsoever.

rules.label: Signed with a public AOSP test key
rules.notes: Private keys for these certificates are published in the AOSP tree, so anyone can forge an update.

rules.label: Signer certificate digest differs from baseline
rules.notes: The definitive certificate-swap check. Compare the SHA-256 of the signer certificate, never the display name, which is trivially forged.

rules.label: More than one signer in the signing block
rules.notes: Valid for key rotation lineage, but also used to keep an original signer visible next to an added one.

rules.label: Application flagged debuggable
rules.notes: Allows a debugger to attach to the process on a production device. Frequently flipped on by patchers.

rules.label: Application flagged testOnly
rules.notes: Set by direct Studio installs. Its presence in a distributed build means the build never went through a release pipeline.

rules.label: Cleartext traffic explicitly permitted
rules.notes: Combined with a redirected endpoint this is what makes plain-HTTP interception of a redirected build possible.

rules.label: Network security config with user trust anchors
rules.notes: Trusting the user certificate store disables pinning and is a common preparation step for traffic capture.

rules.label: extractNativeLibs re-enabled
rules.notes: Modern builds ship uncompressed and page-aligned libraries. Flipping this back on is typical when native libraries were replaced by hand.

rules.label: allowBackup enabled
rules.notes: Permits extraction of the private data directory over adb without root.

rules.label: platformBuildVersionName attribute present
rules.notes: Written by the resource compiler and left untouched by most manifest editors, so it records the original toolchain even after a repack.

rules.label: AGP-derived permission name does not match the application id
rules.notes: AGP generates this permission as applicationId plus a fixed suffix, so its prefix is a second, independent copy of the application id. A manifest editor that rewrites the package attribute almost never rewrites this string, which makes the mismatch a clean rename detector.

rules.label: Application class sits in a machine-generated package
rules.notes: R8 with repackaging moves classes into short generated packages, so the Application class legitimately lives outside the application id. Measured on a clean build as fky.pq.vxdjhbnbm.SztxrmMlumugmyetk. Treat as a build trait, never as tampering, and use it to suppress foreign-package rules.

rules.label: Google Play Billing
rules.notes: In-app purchases present. Worth correlating with patch rules that target purchase verification, since this is the component such patches attack.

rules.label: Play services and datatransport components
rules.notes: Pulled in transitively by Firebase and Play libraries. Listed explicitly so these classes can be excluded from foreign-package heuristics.

rules.label: AndroidX core component factory
rules.notes: Standard AGP output. Its absence in an androidx-based app suggests a rewritten manifest.

rules.label: OpenGL ES version requirement
rules.notes: Declared as a packed hex value: 0x20000 is ES 2.0, 0x30000 is ES 3.0. Useful for corroborating an engine guess from the native ruleset.

rules.label: Wide gap between minSdkVersion and targetSdkVersion
rules.notes: Measured 21 to 36 on a clean build, so this is common and must stay low. It matters only as context: a low minSdk keeps weaker platform defaults such as cleartext traffic and v1-only signature acceptance reachable.

rules.label: compileSdkVersion higher than targetSdkVersion
rules.notes: Normal during platform transitions. Recorded because compileSdkVersion and platformBuildVersion together pin the build toolchain even after a repack.

structural_heuristics.label: Duplicate entries in the global string pool
structural_heuristics.notes: aapt2 deduplicates the value pool, so a clean release build reports exactly zero duplicates. Any duplicate means the pool was serialized by something other than aapt2.

structural_heuristics.label: Data past the declared ResTable size
structural_heuristics.notes: The root chunk size must equal the file size. Extra bytes are either an appended payload or a sloppy in-place edit.

structural_heuristics.label: Type spec entry count disagrees with type chunk entry count
structural_heuristics.notes: Adding or removing entries without updating the matching spec chunk is a very common hand-editing mistake.

structural_heuristics.label: lastPublicType or lastPublicKey is non-zero
structural_heuristics.notes: aapt2 writes zero in both fields. Non-zero points at the legacy aapt or a hand-built table.

structural_heuristics.label: Type string pool encoded as UTF-8
structural_heuristics.notes: aapt2 emits UTF-16 type names while key and value pools are UTF-8. A UTF-8 type pool means the table was re-serialized.

structural_heuristics.label: Sorted flag set on the global string pool
structural_heuristics.notes: Release builds leave the value pool unsorted. The sorted flag indicates a rebuild by another writer.

structural_heuristics.label: More than one package chunk
structural_heuristics.notes: Normal for shared libraries and overlays, unusual for an application. Merged tables show up this way.

structural_heuristics.label: Shared library reference chunk present
structural_heuristics.notes: Records dynamic package id remapping. Record the referenced package names as part of the inventory.

structural_heuristics.label: Almost no locale-qualified configs despite many string entries
structural_heuristics.notes: Low severity on purpose. Engine games legitimately keep translations in their own asset bundles, so this is context, not a verdict.

structural_heuristics.label: Resource file paths flattened to short names
structural_heuristics.notes: Produced by the AGP resource path shortening optimization. Useful as a build-identity trait, not as a tamper signal.

structural_heuristics.label: Sparse or 16-bit offset entry encoding in use
structural_heuristics.notes: Modern aapt2 space optimizations. Their absence in a build whose baseline used them suggests a downgrade through an older tool.

structural_heuristics.label: Placeholder name for an unused type id
structural_heuristics.notes: aapt2 fills gaps in the type id space with a synthetic name. Expected in real builds and worth whitelisting so it never counts as an anomaly.

structural_heuristics.label: Data past the declared AXML size
structural_heuristics.notes: Root chunk size must equal the file size. Measured exactly 0 on a clean build.

structural_heuristics.label: Duplicate entries in the AXML string pool
structural_heuristics.notes: Threshold is 1, not 0: a clean measured manifest already carries one duplicate because raw attribute values and element names share the pool. This is why the resources.arsc duplicate rule cannot be reused verbatim here.

structural_heuristics.label: AXML string pool is not UTF-8
structural_heuristics.notes: aapt2 writes a UTF-8 pool for manifests. UTF-16 indicates a different writer.

structural_heuristics.label: No resource map chunk despite framework attributes
structural_heuristics.notes: The 0x0180 chunk maps attribute indices to framework resource ids. Measured 25 entries on a clean build. Some rebuild tools drop it, which still installs but loses the mapping.

structural_heuristics.label: More namespace declarations than expected
structural_heuristics.notes: A plain app manifest declares only the android namespace. Extra ones appear when tooling merges in distribution or overlay attributes.
